B1:
Touched fires many times per contact (each body part, every physics step of overlap), and the events queue before part:Destroy() takes effect/replicates, so several handlers run and award 10 each. There's no debounce. Fix: guard with a flag set before awarding:
```lua
local part = script.Parent
local collected = false
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
  if collected then return end
  local plr = game.Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
  if not plr then return end
  collected = true
  local coins = plr:FindFirstChild('leaderstats') and plr.leaderstats:FindFirstChild('Coins')
  if coins then coins.Value += 10 end
  part:Destroy()
end)
```
Run it on the server; for respawning coins use a per-player/per-coin cooldown instead of Destroy.
B2: With StreamingEnabled the client only has parts near the player; far-away buildings (and their Door) aren't streamed in yet, so direct indexing workspace.Map.Buildings.Hotel.Door errors. Even WaitForChild may yield forever and streamed parts can stream out later. Fixes: (1) Tag doors with CollectionService and use GetInstanceAddedSignal('Door') plus GetTagged/GetInstanceRemovedSignal, so handlers connect whenever a door streams in and clean up when it streams out. (2) Make the door model ModelStreamingMode = Atomic (or Persistent if truly needed) and use WaitForChild with a timeout / ChildAdded, or call player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(position) before accessing. Better still, do door Touched logic on the server, where everything exists.
B3: Bugs: (1) Returns PurchaseGranted even if pcall failed, so a failed save = charged with nothing. (2) No PurchaseId idempotency: if the callback runs again (retry, rejoin, server crash after save but before ack) coins are granted twice. (3) plr may be nil (player left) -> plr.UserId errors inside pcall -> still returns Granted. (4) GetAsync + SetAsync is a non-atomic read-modify-write that can clobber concurrent writes; ProductId isn't checked. Correct behaviour: if player not present return NotProcessedYet; use UpdateAsync (or session-locked profile) that, in one atomic write, checks a stored list of processed PurchaseIds, adds 100 coins and records the PurchaseId; only if that write succeeds return PurchaseGranted, otherwise return NotProcessedYet so Roblox retries; only one script assigns ProcessReceipt; unknown ProductId -> NotProcessedYet; update the in-memory/leaderstats value after the save.
B4: Remote arguments are serialized: tables are copied as plain data, metatables are stripped, so the client receives {Name='Rifle', Ammo=30} without __index and w:Fire is nil. Functions also can't be sent. Instances are sent as references, and ServerStorage contents never replicate to clients, so the Muzzle reference arrives as nil. Fix: send plain data (e.g. weapon id/state) and reconstruct the object on the client with a shared ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage (setmetatable(data, Weapon) / Weapon.new(data)); put assets the client needs in ReplicatedStorage (or a replicated workspace location), or send an identifier and let the client find its own copy.
B5:
workspace:Raycast's second argument is the direction vector including length; dir is a unit vector, so the ray is only 1 stud long. Also ignore the shooter's character. Fix:
```lua
local dir = (target - origin).Unit * 500 -- max range
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {shooterCharacter}
local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if r then print(r.Instance) end
```
(or use target - origin directly for an exact-length ray).
B6: When the last player leaves, the server starts shutting down; PlayerRemoving may run but the server closes before the async SetAsync completes (or fires too late), so the save is killed. Standard fix: game:BindToClose(function() ... end) that saves every remaining player's data (in parallel with task.spawn and waits for all, within the ~30 s limit), plus a guard so PlayerRemoving and BindToClose don't double-save; use UpdateAsync with retries and periodic autosave so little is lost even on crash. In Studio, BindToClose may need to skip or wait briefly.

```lua
local MPS = game:GetService('MarketplaceService')
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local store = game:GetService('DataStoreService'):GetDataStore('PlayerData')
local GEMS100 = 123456

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info) -- only script that sets this
  if info.ProductId ~= GEMS100 then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local plr = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  if not plr then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end -- retried next join
  local pid = tostring(info.PurchaseId)
  local ok, data = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, 'u_' .. info.PlayerId, function(d)
    d = d or {Gems = 0, Receipts = {}}
    d.Receipts = d.Receipts or {}
    if d.Receipts[pid] then return d end -- already granted: idempotent
    d.Gems += 100
    d.Receipts[pid] = os.time() -- prune old entries periodically
    return d
  end)
  if not ok or not data then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  if plr.Parent then plr:SetAttribute('Gems', data.Gems) end
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end
```
If you use a session-locked profile, write gems + PurchaseId into it and return Granted only after it saves.

```lua
local TweenService = game:GetService('TweenService')
local info = TweenInfo.new(0.4, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local SHOWN = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0)
local HIDDEN = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1.5, 0)
local current

local function open()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  menu.Position = HIDDEN
  menu.Visible = true
  current = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = SHOWN})
  current:Play()
end

local function close()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  local t = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = HIDDEN})
  current = t
  t.Completed:Connect(function(state)
    if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and current == t then
      menu.Visible = false
    end
  end)
  t:Play()
end
```

```lua
local MAX_RANGE, DAMAGE = 200, 20
local function shoot(player: Player, targetPos: Vector3)
  if typeof(targetPos) ~= 'Vector3' or targetPos ~= targetPos then return end
  local char = player.Character
  local head = char and char:FindFirstChild('Head')
  local myHum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if not head or not myHum or myHum.Health <= 0 then return end
  local origin = head.Position
  local offset = targetPos - origin

  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {char}

  if not result then return end
  local model = result.Instance:FindFirstAncestorOfClass('Model')
  local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if hum and hum.Health > 0 then
    hum:TakeDamage(DAMAGE)
  end
end
```

```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService('CollectionService')
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local TAG = 'KillBrick'
local conns = {} -- [part] = connection

local function onAdded(part)
  if not part:IsA('BasePart') or conns[part] then return end
  conns[part] = part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local hum = hit.Parent and hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
    if hum and hum.Health > 0 then hum.Health = 0 end
  end)
end

local function onRemoved(part)
  local c = conns[part]
  if c then c:Disconnect(); conns[part] = nil end
end

CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TAG):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TAG):Connect(onRemoved)
for _, p in CollectionService:GetTagged(TAG) do onAdded(p) end
```
(Removed signal also fires when the part is destroyed, so the table doesn't leak.)

B13: (a) Client -> server purchase: a RemoteFunction (or RemoteEvent) 'BuySword' that sends only the item id. The server validates everything (item exists, price from server config, balance sufficient, rate limit), deducts coins and grants the sword; the balance lives on the server (player data/leaderstats or attribute) and is the single source of truth. The RemoteFunction can return success/reason to the client. (b) Server -> client counter: a RemoteEvent FireClient('CoinsChanged', newBalance), or simply replicate the value via leaderstats IntValue / player attribute and have the UI listen to .Changed / GetAttributeChangedSignal. Don't use server-to-client InvokeClient: the server yields waiting for the client, which can hang forever, error if the client leaves, or be exploited (client never returns or returns garbage), stalling server logic; UI updates need no reply anyway.
B14: Teleport data (TeleportOptions:SetTeleportData) is sent through the client, so it is readable and modifiable by exploiters, has size limits and can be lost if the teleport fails - fine only for non-authoritative info (selected map, party id, cosmetic loadout choice). DataStores are authoritative and persistent but have request budgets and latency, and the destination may load before the source finished saving (need session locking/save-before-teleport). MemoryStores (HashMap/SortedMap) are fast, cross-server and short-lived (TTL) - good for transient match state/handoff. Choice: keep the coin balance in a session-locked DataStore profile: save and release the lock before TeleportAsync, load in the match place (waiting for release). Pass the loadout choice either as teleport data validated server-side against owned items, or via MemoryStore keyed by userId; never trust teleported coins.
B15: Per-instance Scripts: 610 copies of near-identical code, each with its own thread/memory and connections; bug fixes need editing every copy (or packages), hard to version, harder to profile, slower load, and instances cloned at runtime need scripts cloned too. Tag-driven: tag instances ('Door', 'Pickup', 'Turret') with CollectionService and have one server Script/ModuleScript per type (e.g. ServerScriptService/Systems/DoorSystem). Each system: process GetTagged(tag), connect GetInstanceAddedSignal(tag) to set up (connections stored in a table keyed by instance) and GetInstanceRemovedSignal(tag) to disconnect/clean up; per-instance config via attributes. Newly spawned instances are handled automatically when tagged (tag in the template). On the client with StreamingEnabled, instances streaming in/out fire the added/removed signals, so client visual systems (door animations, pickup spin) set up and clean up naturally; make tagged models Atomic so descendants arrive together. Server keeps authority (turret targeting/damage, pickup grants); turrets can share one update loop.
B16: Give the driver's client network ownership of the car (VehicleSeat auto-ownership, or SetNetworkOwner(driver) when they sit; server/anchored when parked or empty, re-set after unanchoring) so physics and input feel responsive without latency. Risk: the owning client simulates the car's physics, so an exploiter can set any position/velocity - speed hacks, teleporting to the finish, flinging other cars, noclipping through walls. The server must still validate: speed and acceleration vs. car stats, displacement per tick (teleport detection), checkpoint order and lap/finish timing, plausible positions (not inside walls/off track), and handle exceptions it causes itself (boost pads, respawns). Respond with strikes: reset/rubber-band the car, revoke ownership (server-owned), then kick. Award results only from server-validated data. The newer alternative is Server Authority mode with client prediction.
B17: Use an UnreliableRemoteEvent for the aim/position stream (and consider lowering to 10-20 Hz, sending only on meaningful change, quantizing values, and interpolating). Constraints: delivery is not guaranteed and not ordered, and payloads over about 1 KB (~900 bytes) are dropped silently. Handle them by: making every packet a full snapshot (not deltas), including a sequence number/timestamp and discarding older or duplicate packets server-side, keeping payloads tiny (Vector3s/compact numbers, buffers, no strings/tables), and using a normal RemoteEvent for anything that must arrive (fire start/stop, hits, purchases). Still validate types, NaN and magnitude on the server and rate-limit.
B18: Split NPCs across many Actors (e.g. 16-64 Actors, each owning a batch of NPCs with its script inside the Actor, more Actors than cores). Each Actor runs its per-frame work with RunService.Heartbeat:ConnectParallel (or BindToMessageParallel via Actor:SendMessage): in the parallel phase do raycasts (workspace:Raycast is parallel-safe), read positions and score paths, writing results into Lua locals or a SharedTable; then call task.synchronize() and apply results serially (set CFrames, Humanoid:MoveTo, fire events); task.desynchronize() to go back. Limitations: in parallel you can read most of the DataModel but cannot write instance properties or call most non-thread-safe APIs (writes must happen after synchronize); each Actor has its own Lua VM, so module state isn't shared - pass data with SendMessage (copied) or SharedTable (use SharedTable.increment/update atomics); require modules at load; Actor scripts must be descendants of the Actor; overhead means batching matters; pathfinding service calls may not be parallel-safe; profile with MicroProfiler first and consider reducing frequency (stagger NPCs, lower tick rates for distant NPCs).
B19: Turn on Workspace.StreamingEnabled (set in Studio Properties). Sensible settings: StreamingMinRadius around 64 (default), StreamingTargetRadius ~ 1024 default, lower (e.g. 256-512) for heavy mobile maps; StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic; StreamingIntegrityMode = PauseOutsideLoadedArea (or MinimumRadiusPause); ModelStreamingBehavior = Improved; set ModelStreamingMode = Atomic on interactable models/vehicles, Persistent only for tiny essentials, PersistentPerPlayer for a player's own car. Scripts: client code must not assume parts exist - replace direct indexing with CollectionService added/removed signals or WaitForChild on Atomic models, handle stream-out (cleanup when instances vanish), use player:RequestStreamAroundAsync before teleporting/cutscenes and Player:AddReplicationFocus for look-ahead, handle Player.GameplayPaused, and keep authoritative logic on the server where everything exists. Test on a low-end phone.
B20: Each SetAsync is a write request; 80 players every 5 s = ~960 writes/min, far above the write budget (60 + 10 x players per server under the old per-server limits; per-experience 300 + 20 x CCU now), and the per-key write rate (one write per key ~every 6 s) is also hit. Requests that exceed the budget are queued; once a request type's queue is full (30) further requests are dropped with error 302, losing saves. SetAsync also blindly overwrites. Better: autosave every 60-120 s (or only dirty data), staggered per player with a random offset so writes don't burst; use UpdateAsync with session locking; save on PlayerRemoving and BindToClose; check DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before writing and back off; bounded pcall retries with delays; keep fast-changing data in memory (or MemoryStore) and persist periodically.
B21: Enable it in Studio's Assistant: open Manage MCP Servers and turn on 'Enable Studio as MCP server', then configure the external client (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) to connect to it and restart the client after editing config. It exposes ~25 tools, e.g. list_roblox_studios, get_studio_state, execute_luau, script_read, script_grep, multi_edit, search_game_tree, inspect_instance, search_asset, insert_asset, start_stop_play, get_console_output, screen_capture. Calls target a studio_id (changes when Studio restarts).
B22: Three core instances: InputContext (a group of actions with Enabled, Priority and Sink), InputAction (one mechanic, Type Bool / Direction1D / Direction2D / Direction3D / ViewportPosition) and InputBinding (one device mapping under an action: KeyCode, UIButton for touch, etc.). A Bool action signals a press via InputAction.Pressed (and Released); all types fire StateChanged, and GetState() can be polled for analog values. For a menu, create a menu InputContext with a higher Priority than the gameplay/default player-script contexts and Sink = true, and enable it while the menu is open, so its bindings consume the input and lower-priority contexts (the default player controls, when Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem is on) don't receive it; disable it on close.
B23: It's the UI Styling system (StyleSheets, edited in the Style Editor, beta). Instances: StyleSheet (holds StyleRules and tokens), StyleRule (a Selector plus property values via SetProperties/SetProperty - selectors match class, tag, name, modifiers, GuiState like :hover), StyleDerive (makes a sheet inherit another), StyleLink (connects a StyleSheet to a ScreenGui/UI tree; its descendants receive the rules) and StyleQuery (conditional rules, e.g. by size or preferred input). Styles reach UI through a StyleLink under the ScreenGui (or a parent) referencing the sheet; rules apply to matching descendants, cascading with specificity. Tokens: define attributes on a token StyleSheet (e.g. PrimaryColor) and reference them in rules as '$PrimaryColor'; themes are sheets with the same token names swapped at runtime. Don't set the same property from code and styles.
B24: Chat requires an age check, usually via facial age estimation through the Roblox app (selfie video, processed by a vendor; ID verification or parental controls can correct it). Players are placed in age groups: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20, 21+. Players can chat only with their own group and the adjacent groups (e.g. 13-15 can chat with 9-12, 13-15, 16-17), except Trusted Connections they know; under-9s need parental consent and chat is off by default for the youngest; users who haven't completed the check can't use chat. Games get no age API; chat is hidden from those who may not receive it, so design gameplay not to depend on chat.
